leave.title: Save before leaving?
leave.body: Kept on this device, they are offered again next time you edit this page, for seven days. Nothing is written until they are saved.

conflict.message: This page changed outside the builder since it was opened. Keep your version to write it over those changes, or reload and drop yours.

connect_prompt.title: Start from a database you already run
connect_prompt.description: Connect it and the builder turns its tables into pages, written as code in your project.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: Name a connection and give its URL. The URL is written to your .env, never to the configuration. In a git project, only where git ignores that file. A read-only role is enough to start.

map.title: Map
map.text_assistant: The assistant reads the schema (tables, fields, relations) and aggregates such as counts, ranges and the values of short lists like statuses. Its database tools return no row.
map.text_manual: The builder reads the schema and the same aggregates, then proposes a mapping. You review it yourself, table by table, with a few sample rows shown to you alone, before any page is generated.

build.title: Build
build.text: A back office as code you own. Pages are written into your project as TypeScript and start read-only.

connect_prompt.later: You can connect a database later from the Database workspace of the builder.

toasts.copy_failed: Could not copy to the clipboard
toasts.locked: This setting or placement is managed in code and cannot be changed here
toasts.period_added: Added a period selector at the top of the page, for the card to follow

add.undeclared: The configuration does not declare this connection.

add.done_variable: Written into the configuration, the URL into .env as {variable}. Every deployed environment sets it where it keeps its secrets, never in git.

reload.title: Reloading the project
reload.gave_up: The project did not come back within 3 minutes. Restart it by hand: stop the process running the project, then start it again.
reload.running: The project reloads to load the connection. This takes about 15 seconds.

applied.building: The assistant is building the dashboard and the pages' details.
applied.hand_off: Let the assistant build the dashboard

copy.label: Copy prompt
copy.agent: Run this work in your own agent, Claude Code or Codex, instead of the chatbox. The agent needs the AntelopeJS plugin, which syncs the skills your project's modules ship.
copy.skills: The prompt names dms-external-database and dms-page-design. They ship with dms-ai, so the project needs that module for the plugin to sync them.
copy.docs: Read how to set it up

connect.options: Other options, kept from the pasted URL:
connect.env: Written into the project's .env as {variable}, never into the configuration.
connect.env_database: Written into the project's .env as {variable}, the database as {databaseVariable}, never into the configuration.
connect.driver_help: The {package} instance that connects to this database.
connect.tables_help: The module the database's tables and pages are written into.
connect.variable_help: Holds the URL in each environment.
connect.database_variable_help: Holds the database name in each environment.
connect.show_changes_hint: What Connect writes, before it does.

edit.unreadable: The connection's URL could not be read from .env.
edit.database_help: Read from its own variable in .env.
edit.password_needed: Another server or user: enter its password.

remove.title: Remove {connection}
remove.intro: Takes the database out of the project. The database itself is not touched.
remove.driver_and_modules: remove the driver {driver} and the module {modules} from antelope.config.ts, so its pages are no longer served;
remove.modules: remove the module {modules} from antelope.config.ts, so its pages are no longer served;
remove.keep_driver: keep the driver {driver} and its URL: it is the project's own database, or another module reads through it;
remove.keep_modules: keep {modules}: it reads through the driver but does not record this connection, so it was not made for it;
remove.delete_folders: delete {folders}, with the tables and pages written there;
remove.remove_connection: remove the {connection} connection of the builder and dms-ai;

engines.postgres_account: A role with SELECT on the schemas to map, and writes only where pages edit.
engines.mongodb_account: A user with the built-in read role, and writes only on the collections pages edit.
engines.rethinkdb_account: A user with read permission on the database, and write only on the tables pages edit.

statsOnly.help: Stats pages can count and chart it.

excluded.help: Not mapped, and not proposed again.

relation.label_help: The column a row is named by. It shows {where}.
relation.sampled_empty: {empty} of {rows} sampled rows has nothing to show here. | {empty} of {rows} sampled rows have nothing to show here.
relation.sample_note: Up to {limit} rows, shown here only and never passed on.

server.schemas: The database has {count} tables, more than one analysis reads at once, so none were read yet. Pick the schemas to analyse.
server.label: Which column names a row of {relation}? It is what its list shows first, and what columns of other tables pointing at it show.
server.purpose: What should {relation} become? Its names, comments and data do not say what it holds.

lossy.bigint: a bigint beyond 2^53 loses precision as a number; declare it string to read it exactly
lossy.numeric: a numeric loses precision as a number; declare it string to read it exactly
lossy.real: a real widened to a number is not the decimal it was written as
lossy.json: json is read as jsonb: duplicate keys, key order and whitespace are not kept
lossy.timestamp: a timestamp without time zone is read as UTC; {rest}

rules.R1: The database reports this table cannot be read.
rules.R2: No key: it can feed stats, not a page.
rules.R4: A framework's or a migration tool's table.
rules.R5: It only links two other tables: for stats only.
rules.R6: It has a key, rows and a column that names a row: a page.
rules.R7: Other tables point at it but no column names a row: a page, its rows named by their key.
rules.R8: Dated rows and nothing that names a row: events or a log, for stats only.
rules.R9: Nothing in the data says what it holds.
rules.L1: A column named like a person's or a thing's name, then the column whose name best fits a row name, then the first such column.
rules.L2: From the database's comment when it is short, otherwise from the name.
rules.F1: No column type can read it.
rules.F3: The first type the column can be read as.
rules.F4: The database declares it points at a table with a page.
rules.F5: Every value matches a row of the other table, though the database does not declare it.
rules.FL: From what the data looks like.
rules.D1: Every value of this text column is one of a few: a badge, one tone per value.
rules.D2: A number named like an amount: shown as a price.
rules.D3: Named after the table it points at, in singular.
rules.T1: Tabs on the column that tells a status.
